newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end weaker on hedges, Brazil crops.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end weaker on hedges, Brazil crops.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower on Wednesday on commercial hedging amid reports of active crop movement in Brazil, traders said.
"Talk of big bean movement in northern Brazil, the biggest yet," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. "There was talk the crushers there were hedging some of their purchases here."

Funds were ambivalent toward soybeans which further depressed the market that had been watchful of another fund buying spree. Tuesday's surprise fund activity sent nearbys surging half the 30-cent daily trading limit and traders said sellers had been nervous early Wednesday.
Commercials were mostly sellers of the March which traders attributed to hedges. Farmer sales picked up after Tuesday's sharp rally. Floor sources also reported active hedging from Brazilian traders.
Private consultant Safras e Mercado said four percent of Brazil's soybean crop had been harvested as of February 20, slightly above the five-year average of three percent.
Demand for soybeans was very strong from crushers and exporters eager to load ships for export, CBOT traders said.
Soybeans closed 8-1/2 to four cents per bushel lower with March off 7-1/4 at $7.83-3/4.
At Brazil's key Paranagua port, three ships were loading soymeal on Wednesday and 14 others were waiting to load soybeans and soymeal, port authorities said.

The March contract was under pressure ahead of first notice day for deliveries on Friday. Traders disagreed on how much would be delivered against the March with estimates ranging from zero to two million bushels.

On the day, ADM sold at least 1.5 million bushels March and one million May while Continental Grain sold one million March. Goldenberg-Hehmeyer sold four million May and Prudential Securities sold 2.5 million May, traders said.
In options trade, Continental Grain bought 200 May $8.00 calls and sold 200 May $8.50 calls at 13 cents.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 80,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 96,201 contracts.
